newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips says dividend policy unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Philips says dividend policy unchanged.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Thursday it had no plans to change its dividend policy despite a disastrous third quarter which has prompted an acceleration of a swingeing restructuring programme.

"We made a statement when we reintroduced the dividend in 1993 that we were introducing (one) that we believed would be able to be sustainable through good times and bad," finance director Dudley Eustace told a news conference.
"We have no reason to change that view," he added.
Philips paid out 1.60 guilders per share in full-year 1995.
The company earlier announced third-quarter net profit from normal operations of 123 million guilders versus 539 million in the year-earlier quarter.

Philips also said it would take a further one billion guilder gross restructuring charge in the current fourth quarter, on top of an earlier 800 million guilder charge to restructure its Sound & Vision unit announced in July.
-- Lien van der Leij, A'dam newsroom +31 220 504 5000.
